sourceInformation.source: The Wire (2002-2008), kept as gritty and real as the show. Original characters and places.
sourceInformation.genre: Investigation / stealth / action-adventure (surveillance, listening and case-building, then a raid)
sourceInformation.perspective: Three-quarter top-down (engine native); V or R3 switches to top-down or isometric. Menus and the wire room are flat screens.
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.1 handoff (single-file engine, TileMap, Mover, Humanoid rigs, Suspicion, Dialog, Menu, Bullets, FlowField, canvas lighting, rain); AI Hub session client 1.3.0; plain JavaScript, no other libraries.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Engine native pixel art at 320x240 expanded to any screen: HD-shaded Humanoid rigs, brick and plaster blocks, rain, streetlamp and flashlight lighting.
sourceInformation.animation: Engine native: procedural Humanoid rigs (poses, expressions, live dialog portraits), tweened UI, particles, hit effects.
sourceInformation.audio: All code-written: six synthesised music loops, synth sound effects, and Animalese-style gibberish voices (a note per typed letter, pitched per speaker). No audio files.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, parallel mode (1-4 players, own copy each, score reported); passes the hub harness check. No other networking.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium and WebKit through Playwright: scripted full playthrough by the attract-mode AI, keyboard tests of photos, tip, tap, wire logging and raid, a mocked DualSense for axis inversion and glyphs, touch emulation, viewport-matrix (13 viewports, WebKit), hub harness. No real controller or iOS Safari.
sourceInformation.research: Read the engine card, the stealth and adventure kits and the hub protocol. No web research on the show; written from general knowledge.
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: About 9: an unreachable room (a table blocked a doorway), attract mode stalling on dialog, symbols the font cannot draw (several), cuff range lost after a shove, an enemy facing away with no gun, a menu hiding the title cast, a tagline cut off on phones, and a stale test server.
2 critical: the blocked doorway made the raid unfinishable, and the demo froze on the judge's dialog.
The attract-mode run: the demo plays the whole case, so one scripted pass hit every scene and found both critical bugs.
Full-page screenshots of every viewport: only the title screen was reachable there, so they showed layout but few bugs.
engineFeedback: Humanoid rigs with live dialog portraits, and the free pause, settings, controls and glyph options; Mover, sees and Suspicion gave stealth almost for free.
Yes. I guessed the font had pad symbols (it does not), that game.go switches at once (it fades first), and that input.tap is keyboard (it flips prompts to touch).
The wire-room listening game, the case board, raid combat, the attract-mode driver, pixel-drawn pad symbols, and a gamepad axis-inversion shim.
Building non-world screens: the canvas UI kit is thin for text-heavy or card screens, and FlowField treats any tall prop as a wall.
The split between the canvas Menu and the HTML settings screens; one UI system would be simpler.
Add built-in gamepad axis inversion and a font that includes controller face-button symbols.
promptFeedback: Clear deliverables, the controller-first rules, and the exit-interview JSON that tools read.
Whether the source name includes the phrase after the dash, the 50-titles-then-RNG step (the list is not checkable), and how Online and Multiplayer differ.
Scope: a feature-complete slice with attract mode, hub play and a 10-foot UI, tested only in headless browsers.
Play the whole game start to finish with a real DualSense on a TV.
